## 1. Introduction

**Project overview.** Interlude is a social music platform in the music-streaming and social-listening domain. Listeners currently lack a simple way to discover music and listen together with others in real time, and independent musicians lack an easy way to see how their music is being listened to. Interlude addresses both problems in one web application: a music catalogue with search and a player, shared listening rooms with synchronized playback, real-time presence and text chat, and a musician dashboard that shows basic listening statistics. A native mobile application provides the core listening features (login, search/browse and playback). A small AI-powered music-discovery assistant is an optional goal that will only be considered after the core requirements are complete.

**Purpose of this document.** This Requirements Specification describes *what* Interlude must do and the quality constraints it must satisfy. It turns the features and tasks defined in the Project Plan (v2, Sections 1.2–1.4 and 2) into uniquely identified, verifiable requirements, and describes who uses the system and how. It is the reference for the Requirement Analysis, Software Design and Software Test reports, and for acceptance testing of the deliverables. All task (`T-##`), deliverable (`D-##`) and work-breakdown (`WBS-#.#`) IDs used here are the ones defined in the Project Plan.

**Structure of the document.**

- **Section 2 — System Requirements** lists the functional requirements (`FR-##`), each linked to its Project Plan task and deliverable with a priority and acceptance condition, followed by the non-functional requirements (`NFR-##`) derived from the quality attributes in Project Plan Section 1.4.
- **Section 3 — Use Cases** defines the user types (`UT-##`) and personas (`P-##`), narrates user scenarios (`SC-##`), gives a user story for every WBS activity, shows use case diagrams for the whole system and for each major functionality, and specifies each use case (`UC-##`) in detail with main, alternative and exception flows. A coverage matrix (Section 3.4.1) shows that every Project Plan task is covered.

**Priority scale.** *Must* = required for the core release v1.0; *Should* = planned for v1.0 but can be cut under schedule pressure without breaking a deliverable's acceptance criterion; *Could* = optional scope (only T-18 / D-10).

**Functional requirement notes:**

- **Roles.** A *musician* has all the capabilities of a *listener* plus catalogue management and the dashboard. *Room host* is not an account role; it is a temporary role inside one listening room (see Section 3.1).
- **Account type at registration (FR-03).** Users choose listener or musician when registering. Admin accounts are not available through registration; they are created by the team (e.g., via Django's admin command) or assigned by another admin (FR-10).
- **Guest access.** Apart from registration and login, all features require authentication, because streaming URLs and listening events are tied to a user.
- **Values still to agree on.** The password policy (FR-04), and the allowed audio/image file types and the maximum upload size (FR-17) have not been fixed yet. They will be agreed by the module owners and recorded in the Design Specification; this document deliberately does not invent them.
- **Real-time technologies (FR-29–FR-34).** Room chat and presence use WebSocket, and room audio is streamed with WebRTC; both belong to the real-time module (listening rooms, presence, chat and synchronized playback). The WebSocket-coordinated fallback of risk R-10 remains the Project Plan contingency if WebRTC streaming proves infeasible.
- **Listening events (FR-35)** are produced by both the web player and the mobile player and are created as a side effect of playback (included in UC-09, UC-13 and UC-16). A play counts toward the musician's statistics only after 30 seconds of listening (FR-36).
- **Rooms (FR-26–FR-28, FR-49–FR-51).** Every room holds at most 10 participants. Public rooms are joined by selecting them in the room list; private rooms and searching rooms by name are a *Should* feature.
- **Copyright reports (FR-11, FR-52).** Reports are submitted from the musician's profile. When an admin removes the reported content, the uploader's account is deactivated and the user cannot ask the admin to reactivate or approve it again.
- **Dependencies.** FR-23 depends on FR-17 (stored media); FR-32 depends on FR-23 and FR-29; FR-36–FR-39 and FR-53 depend on FR-35; FR-48 depends on FR-47.

### 2.2 Non-functional Requirements

| Requirement ID | Quality attribute | Non-functional requirement (natural language) | Applies to | Verification / measurement |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| NFR-01 | Security | The system shall store passwords only as Argon2 hashes and shall never store or log passwords in plain text. | FR-03, FR-05 | Unit test checks the stored hash uses the Argon2 hasher; code review of logging. |
| NFR-02 | Security | All REST endpoints except registration and login, and all WebSocket connections, shall require authentication, and all authorization decisions shall be made on the server (hiding UI elements is not sufficient). | Whole system; FR-08, FR-09 | Permission tests call every protected endpoint directly without/with wrong-role tokens. |
| NFR-03 | Security | The deployed system shall be reachable only over HTTPS (and WSS for WebSockets). | Deployment; FR-43 | Plain HTTP requests to the production URL are redirected or refused; configuration review. |
| NFR-04 | Security | Media files shall be served only through time-limited storage URLs; storage containers shall not be publicly listable. | FR-17, FR-23 | Test: expired URL is refused; anonymous access to the container fails. |
| NFR-05 | Security | Secrets (keys, passwords, connection strings) shall be kept out of the repository and supplied through environment variables or Azure configuration. | Whole system | Secret scanning runs in CI; review of repository history. |
| NFR-06 | Security | Uploaded files shall be validated on the server by type and size, regardless of client-side checks. | FR-17 | Tests send disallowed and oversized files directly to the API. |
| NFR-07 | Performance | Catalogue and search API requests shall respond in under 500 ms under demo load. | FR-20, FR-21, FR-22 | Timed API tests and a load script with 20 simulated users against staging. |
| NFR-08 | Performance | A chat message shall be delivered to the other participants of a room in under 300 ms under demo load. | FR-30 | Multi-client timing test with timestamps on send and receive. |
| NFR-09 | Performance | The playback position of all participants in a room shall differ from the host's by less than 500 ms. | FR-32, FR-33 | Measured drift in a multi-client room test. |
| NFR-10 | Performance | Playback shall start within 2 s after the user presses play. | FR-23, FR-24, FR-42 | Timed playback test on the deployed system. |
| NFR-11 | Usability | All web pages shall use the shared layout and consistent styling, and the web UI shall be responsive on desktop and mobile browser widths. | All web pages; FR-01 | Page-by-page checklist review; usability walkthrough with 5 peer testers. |
| NFR-12 | Usability | Peer testers shall be able to complete the core flows (log in → find a song → play it; log in → join a room) without help, and every validation or system error shall be shown as a clear message explaining what to do. | UT-02, UT-03 | Usability walkthrough with 5 peer testers; checklist of error messages. |
| NFR-13 | Reliability | WebSocket clients shall reconnect automatically after a lost connection and restore the user's room presence, chat and playback state. | FR-29–FR-34 | Integration test that drops and restores the connection. |
| NFR-14 | Reliability | Failed uploads and failed streams shall be handled gracefully: the user receives an error message and the application remains usable. | FR-17, FR-19, FR-23 | Integration tests of upload and stream error paths. |
| NFR-15 | Reliability | The `main` branch shall always be deployable: merges require a green CI run and an approved review. | Development process; FR-02 | Branch-protection settings review; CI history. |
| NFR-16 | Maintainability | Every pull request shall be reviewed by another team member, code shall pass the configured formatter/linter, and backend test coverage shall be at least 70%. | Whole codebase | CI lint checks; coverage report in CI; PR history. |
| NFR-17 | Maintainability (documentation) | Each module shall be documented in the repository (API endpoints, setup and usage), and the documentation shall be reviewed for consistency with the delivered system. | All modules; T-17 | Documentation review checklist by the documentation coordinator (WBS-17.3, WBS-17.4). |
| NFR-18 | Privacy | Listening data shall be shown to musicians only as aggregates; no individual listener's activity shall be visible to musicians. | FR-36–FR-39 | Review of analytics API responses; tests in FR-39. |
| NFR-19 | Privacy | No personal data shall be sent to an external AI API without a documented privacy review. | FR-44 (optional) | Privacy review document in the optional AI evaluation (WBS-18.1). |
| NFR-20 | Legal / content | Only royalty-free, self-produced or explicitly licensed audio shall be used for testing and the demo. | FR-17, FR-18; demo | Review of the demo dataset before release (risk R-02). |
| NFR-21 | Cost / operational constraint | Cloud resources shall stay within the free/student Azure credits, with budget alerts enabled. | Deployment | Azure budget alerts configured; weekly cost check (risk R-03). |
| NFR-22 | Portability | The mobile application shall run on the platform chosen in WBS-14.1 (on a device or emulator) against the deployed backend API. | FR-40–FR-42 | Manual test of the login → search → play flow on the chosen platform. |

**Non-functional requirement notes / assumptions:**

- **"Demo load"** means 20 simulated concurrent users, as defined in the Project Plan. Performance figures are measured against the staging or production environment on Azure, not on developers' machines. Production-scale load is explicitly out of scope.
- **Supported environments.** The web application targets current desktop and mobile versions of mainstream browsers; the exact list will be confirmed in the Design Specification. The mobile platform and framework are selected in WBS-14.1 (a React-based option such as React Native is expected).
- **Thresholds.** All numeric thresholds above (500 ms, 300 ms, 500 ms drift, 2 s, 70% coverage, 5 testers) come from Project Plan Section 1.4 and Deliverable D-08; no additional thresholds have been introduced.
- **External constraints.** Hosting, database and file storage use Microsoft Azure; the backend is Django with the Django ORM; the web frontend is React with TypeScript.

## 3. Use Cases

### 3.1 User Types

| User type ID | User type / actor | Description and responsibilities | Goals / typical actions | Related requirement ID(s) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| UT-01 | Guest | An unauthenticated visitor of the web or mobile app. | Register an account; log in. | FR-03, FR-04, FR-05, FR-06, FR-40 |
| UT-02 | Listener | A registered user who discovers and listens to music, alone or with others. | Search and browse, play music, manage own profile, follow other users, create playlists, create/join listening rooms, chat, report copyright violations, use the mobile app. | FR-01, FR-05–FR-08, FR-12, FR-13, FR-20–FR-31, FR-33, FR-40–FR-42, FR-44, FR-45–FR-53 |
| UT-03 | Musician | A registered user (often an independent artist) who publishes music. Has all listener capabilities. | Maintain an artist profile, create songs and albums, upload audio and covers, view the analytics dashboard. | FR-13–FR-19, FR-37, FR-38, FR-39 (plus all listener FRs) |
| UT-04 | Room host | A listener or musician who created a listening room or received the host role. A role inside a room, not an account type. | Choose the room's track, play/pause/seek for everyone. | FR-26, FR-28, FR-32, FR-34 |
| UT-05 | Admin | A platform administrator (a team member during the project). | Manage user roles and account status, review copyright reports, remove content that violates rights. | FR-09, FR-10, FR-11, FR-52 |
| UT-06 | CI/CD pipeline (external system) | GitHub Actions pipeline connected to the repository and Azure. | Run lint, tests and coverage on pull requests; deploy tagged releases. | FR-02, FR-43 |
| UT-07 | Azure Blob Storage (external system) | Cloud file storage for audio files and cover images. | Store uploaded files; serve them via time-limited URLs. | FR-17, FR-23 |
| UT-08 | External AI API (external system, optional) | An existing third-party AI API used by the optional assistant. | Interpret natural-language music requests. | FR-44 |

**Access or role distinctions:**

The table below summarizes which account role may perform which action (✓ = allowed, *own* = only on the user's own data, — = not allowed). It is the basis for the permission tests required by FR-09.

| Action | Guest | Listener | Musician | Admin |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Register / log in | ✓ | — | — | — |
| Search, browse, play, use mobile app | — | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ |
| View / edit profile | — | view all public, edit *own* | view all public, edit *own* | view all public, edit *own* |
| Create / join / leave rooms, chat | — | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ |
| Join a private room | — | with password | with password | with password |
| Follow / unfollow users, create playlists | — | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ |
| Show own playlists on profile | — | *own* | *own* | *own* |
| Report a copyright violation | — | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ |
| View copyright reports | — | — | — | ✓ |
| Control room playback | — | host only | host only | host only |
| Create / edit / delete songs and albums, upload files | — | — | *own* | remove any (FR-11) |
| View analytics dashboard | — | — | *own* tracks only | — |
| Change roles, deactivate accounts | — | — | — | ✓ |

Listeners are expected to use the system most frequently and have no technical knowledge; musicians additionally need simple upload and statistics features; admins are rare, technically experienced users. External systems do not use the application UI.

| P-04 | Can, 24 | UT-02 Listener (mobile) | Commutes by metro every day and mostly listens on his phone. |

### 3.2 User Scenarios

| Scenario ID | Title | Persona | Related requirements |
|---|---|---|---|
| SC-01 | Signing up and setting up a profile | P-01 Elif | FR-03–FR-07, FR-12, FR-45–FR-48 |
| SC-02 | Publishing a debut EP | P-02 Mert | FR-13–FR-19 |
| SC-03 | Discovering and playing music | P-01 Elif | FR-01, FR-20–FR-25, FR-35, FR-53 |
| SC-04 | A long-distance listening night | P-01 Elif | FR-08, FR-26–FR-35, FR-49–FR-51 |
| SC-05 | Checking how the EP is doing | P-02 Mert | FR-36–FR-39 |
| SC-06 | Handling a rights complaint | P-03 Deniz | FR-09–FR-11, FR-52 |
| SC-07 | Listening on the commute | P-04 Can | FR-40–FR-42 |
| SC-08 *(optional)* | Asking the assistant for music | P-01 Elif | FR-44 |

**SC-01 — Signing up and setting up a profile**  
**Persona:** P-01 — Elif  
**Related requirements:** FR-03, FR-04, FR-05, FR-06, FR-07, FR-12, FR-45, FR-46, FR-47, FR-48

A friend sends Elif a link to Interlude. She opens it and chooses *Register*. She enters a username, her e-mail and a password, and selects *Listener* as her account type. Her first choice of username is already taken, so the form highlights the field and tells her to choose another. She changes it and submits again; the account is created and she is taken to the login page. She logs in, opens *My Profile*, adds a display name, a short bio and a profile picture, and saves. The profile now shows her new details. She finds the friend who sent her the link, opens his profile and follows him; he now appears in her following list and she appears among his followers. She then creates a playlist called "Study", adds a few songs and chooses to display it on her profile, while keeping a second playlist private. Later, on a shared computer at the library, she logs out so that no one else can use her session. The scenario ends with Elif having a complete profile and a working account.

**SC-02 — Publishing a debut EP**  
**Persona:** P-02 — Mert  
**Related requirements:** FR-13, FR-14, FR-15, FR-16, FR-17, FR-18, FR-19

Mert registers as a *Musician* and fills in his artist profile. He creates a new album called "Night Shift" with a genre, release date and cover image. He then adds four songs: for each one he enters the title and genre, picks the album and track number, selects the audio file and ticks the box confirming he owns the rights. One of his files is in a format the system does not accept, so the upload is rejected with a message listing the allowed types; he exports it again in an allowed format and the upload succeeds. When his Wi-Fi drops during another upload, he sees an error and no broken song is left in his list, so he simply retries. Finally he notices a typo in a song title and corrects it. The scenario ends when the EP appears on Mert's public artist profile and can be found by listeners.

**SC-03 — Discovering and playing music**  
**Persona:** P-01 — Elif  
**Related requirements:** FR-01, FR-20, FR-21, FR-22, FR-23, FR-24, FR-25, FR-35, FR-53

After logging in, Elif lands on the homepage, which shows new releases, including Mert's "Night Shift". She uses the navigation bar to open *Browse* and filters by the electronic genre, paging through the results. She then types "night" into the search bar and sees matching songs, albums and musicians grouped separately. She plays the first song; it starts almost immediately, and the player bar shows the title, artist, cover and elapsed time. She skips ahead to the chorus, adds two more songs to the queue, and lowers the volume. When the song ends, the next queued song starts automatically. Every play, skip and completion is recorded in the background for the musician's statistics. Halfway through a song her Wi-Fi drops; when she is back online, the player offers to resume the same song where she left off, and she continues listening. The scenario ends with Elif listening through her queue.

**SC-04 — A long-distance listening night**  
**Persona:** P-01 — Elif  
**Related requirements:** FR-08, FR-26, FR-27, FR-28, FR-29, FR-30, FR-31, FR-32, FR-33, FR-34, FR-35, FR-49, FR-50, FR-51

On Friday evening Elif creates a private listening room called "Friday Night", sets a password and shares it with her friends; she becomes the room's host. Two friends search for "Friday Night" in the room list, which shows Elif as host and the number of participants, enter the password and join. (Had the room been public, anyone selecting it in the list could have joined without a password.) The room can hold at most 10 people. Each time someone joins, the participant list updates on everyone's screen. Elif picks a song and presses play; her friends hear the same part of the song at the same time. A third friend joins in the middle of the song and starts at the same position as everyone else, and sees the chat messages from the last hour. The group chats about the music while listening. One friend tries to press pause, but only the host can control playback, so nothing changes. When Elif's internet connection drops briefly, her app reconnects automatically and she is back in the room. At the end of the night Elif leaves first, so the host role passes to one of her friends; when the last friend leaves, the room closes. The scenario ends with the room removed from the room list.

**SC-05 — Checking how the EP is doing**  
**Persona:** P-02 — Mert  
**Related requirements:** FR-36, FR-37, FR-38, FR-39

A week after releasing "Night Shift", Mert opens his musician dashboard. He sees the total number of plays (a play counts only when a listener has listened to at least 30 seconds of a track), a chart of plays over time and a list of his tracks ranked by play count, which shows that the second track is clearly the most popular. He changes the time range to the last seven days and all figures update. He can only see aggregated numbers about his own tracks; he cannot see which individual listeners played them or other musicians' statistics. The scenario ends with Mert deciding to promote his most popular track.

**SC-06 — Handling a rights complaint**  
**Persona:** P-03 — Deniz  
**Related requirements:** FR-09, FR-10, FR-11, FR-52

A listener notices that a song on a musician's profile is someone else's copyrighted track. She uses the report option on that musician's profile, writes which song it is and why she thinks it violates copyright, and submits the report. Deniz logs in with her admin account and sees the report in the report list. She checks the song and removes it; it disappears from search results, the musician's profile and any listening room queue, and the account that uploaded it is deactivated. When the account owner tries to log in, the login is refused, and there is no way to ask the admin for approval to reactivate the account. Later, a listener asks for musician access; Deniz changes that user's role to musician, and the user can now upload songs. The scenario ends with the content removed and the accounts in the correct state.

**SC-07 — Listening on the commute**  
**Persona:** P-04 — Can  
**Related requirements:** FR-40, FR-41, FR-42

On his way to work, Can opens the Interlude mobile app and logs in with the same account he uses on the web. He searches for an artist, browses the artist's songs and starts playing one. He pauses when he changes trains and later seeks back a few seconds to hear a part he missed. The scenario ends with Can listening to music on his phone using the same catalogue as the web application.

**SC-08 *(optional)* — Asking the assistant for music**  
**Persona:** P-01 — Elif  
**Related requirements:** FR-44

If the optional assistant is approved, Elif opens it and writes "something calm for studying". The assistant replies with a few songs from the Interlude catalogue, each with a link. She opens one and plays it. If the assistant cannot find a match, it says so instead of inventing songs. The scenario ends with Elif playing a suggested song.

### 3.3 Use Case Diagrams

The diagrams below use UML use case notation drawn with PlantUML: users are shown as stick-figure actors, use cases as ovals, and the rectangle is the system boundary. External systems are shown as boxes marked «system». A line between an actor and a use case is an association; dashed arrows labelled «include» or «extend» show relationships between use cases; a hollow-headed arrow between actors is a generalization (the child actor inherits the parent's use cases). Each diagram is embedded in this file as an image exported from the PlantUML source given below it.

**Whole-system diagram notes:**  
Users are on the left and external systems on the right. *Musician* and *Room host* inherit all listener use cases (generalization); the host additionally controls room playback. *Admin* uses UC-06 only for the removal path (FR-11) and handles copyright reports in UC-19. Project Plan tasks T-15, T-16 and T-17 have no use case (see Section 3.4.1). UC-20 belongs to the optional scope.

```plantuml
skinparam usecaseBorderColor #333333
skinparam rectangleBorderColor #333333
skinparam actorBorderColor #333333
skinparam actorBackgroundColor #FFFFFF
actor "UT-02\nListener" as Listener
actor "UT-03\nMusician" as Musician
rectangle "Analytics and Musician Dashboard" {
  usecase "UC-14: Record listening events" as UC15
  usecase "Aggregate listening metrics\n(plays of at least 30 s)" as Agg
  usecase "UC-15: View musician dashboard" as UC16
  usecase "Filter by time range" as Filter
}
Listener -- UC15 : plays music
Musician -- UC16
UC16 ..> Agg : <<include>>
Filter ..> UC16 : <<extend>>
@enduml
```

</details>

**Functionality covered:** T-12, T-13 / FR-35–FR-39 / UC-14, UC-15  
**Diagram notes:** Listeners trigger UC-14 indirectly by playing music. The dashboard includes the aggregation of events into metrics (FR-36), in which a play counts only after 30 seconds of listening; filtering by time range (FR-38) is an optional extension.

#### 3.4.2 UC-01 — Register an Account

| Field | Description |
|---|---|
| **Use case ID** | UC-01 |
| **Use case name** | Register an account |
| **Goal / Purpose** | A guest wants an account so that they can use Interlude as a listener or musician. |
| **Actor(s)** | UT-01 — Guest |
| **Related Project Plan task(s)** | T-02 |
| **Related functional requirement(s)** | FR-03, FR-04 (NFR-01, NFR-12) |

**Pre-condition(s):**  
The guest is not logged in and has opened the registration page (web or mobile).

**Main success flow:**

1. **Actor:** Enters a username, e-mail address and password and selects the account type (listener or musician).
2. **Actor:** Submits the form.
3. **System:** Validates that the username and e-mail are unused, the e-mail is well-formed and the password meets the password policy.
4. **System:** Creates the account with the selected role and stores the password as an Argon2 hash.
5. **System:** Confirms the registration and redirects the user to the login page.

**Alternative flows:**

- **A1 — Username or e-mail already used (branches from step 3):**
  1. The system finds an existing account with the same username or e-mail.
  2. The system shows a message on the relevant field; no account is created.
  3. The guest corrects the input; the flow returns to step 2.
- **A2 — Invalid e-mail or weak password (branches from step 3):**
  1. The input does not meet the format or password policy.
  2. The system shows a field-level message explaining the rule.
  3. The flow returns to step 2.

**Exception / error flows (if applicable):**

- **E1 — Server error (occurs at step 4):** The system shows a general error message asking the user to try again later; no partial account is created.

**Post-condition(s):**  
A new account exists with exactly one role (listener or musician) and the user can log in with it.

#### 3.4.3 UC-02 — Log In and Log Out

| Field | Description |
|---|---|
| **Use case ID** | UC-02 |
| **Use case name** | Log in and log out |
| **Goal / Purpose** | A registered user wants to access their account securely and end the session when finished. |
| **Actor(s)** | UT-01 — Guest (logging in); UT-02 — Listener, UT-03 — Musician, UT-05 — Admin (logging out) |
| **Related Project Plan task(s)** | T-02 |
| **Related functional requirement(s)** | FR-05, FR-06, FR-07, FR-10 (NFR-02, NFR-03) |

**Pre-condition(s):**  
The user has a registered, active account and is on the login page.

**Main success flow:**

1. **Actor:** Enters username or e-mail and password and submits.
2. **System:** Verifies the credentials and that the account is active.
3. **System:** Issues an authentication token and redirects the user to the homepage, showing the navigation items for the user's role.
4. **Actor:** Uses the application; later selects *Log out*.
5. **System:** Invalidates the token and returns the user to the login page.

**Alternative flows:**

- **A1 — Invalid credentials (branches from step 2):**
  1. The username/e-mail is unknown or the password is wrong.
  2. The system shows the same generic error for both cases and issues no token.
  3. The flow returns to step 1.
- **A2 — Deactivated account (branches from step 2):**
  1. The account has been deactivated by an admin (FR-10).
  2. The system refuses the login and tells the user the account is not active.
  3. The use case ends.
- **A3 — Token expired during use (branches from step 4):**
  1. A request is made with an expired token.
  2. The system rejects it with HTTP 401 and the client redirects to the login page; the flow returns to step 1.

**Exception / error flows (if applicable):**

- **E1 — Authentication service unavailable (occurs at step 2):** The system shows a general error message and the user remains logged out.

**Post-condition(s):**  
After login, the user holds a valid token and sees only features allowed for their role. After logout, the old token is no longer accepted.

#### 3.4.4 UC-03 — Manage User Accounts and Roles

| Field | Description |
|---|---|
| **Use case ID** | UC-03 |
| **Use case name** | Manage user accounts and roles |
| **Goal / Purpose** | The admin wants each account to have the right role and status so that access to features is correct. |
| **Actor(s)** | UT-05 — Admin |
| **Related Project Plan task(s)** | T-03 |
| **Related functional requirement(s)** | FR-09, FR-10 |

**Pre-condition(s):**  
The admin is logged in with an admin account.

**Main success flow:**

1. **Actor:** Opens the user management page.
2. **System:** Verifies the admin role and shows the list of users with their roles and status.
3. **Actor:** Selects a user and changes their role (e.g., listener → musician).
4. **System:** Saves the change and shows the updated role.
5. **System:** Applies the new role's permissions on the user's next request.

**Alternative flows:**

- **A1 — Deactivate or reactivate an account (branches from step 3):**
  1. The admin selects *Deactivate* (or *Reactivate*) for the user.
  2. The system updates the status; a deactivated user's active tokens are invalidated and further logins are refused.
  3. The use case ends.
- **A2 — Non-admin attempts access (branches from step 2):**
  1. A listener or musician opens the page or calls the API.
  2. The system returns HTTP 403 and shows an "access denied" message.
  3. The use case ends.

**Exception / error flows (if applicable):**

- **E1 — Admin tries to remove their own admin role or deactivate themselves (occurs at step 3):** The system rejects the change with an explanation, so that the platform is never left without an admin.

**Post-condition(s):**  
The selected account has the new role or status, and server-side permission checks reflect it.

#### 3.4.5 UC-04 — View and Edit Own Profile

| Field | Description |
|---|---|
| **Use case ID** | UC-04 |
| **Use case name** | View and edit own profile |
| **Goal / Purpose** | The user wants their profile to show up-to-date information about them. |
| **Actor(s)** | UT-02 — Listener, UT-03 — Musician |
| **Related Project Plan task(s)** | T-04 |
| **Related functional requirement(s)** | FR-12, FR-09 |

**Pre-condition(s):**  
The user is logged in.

**Main success flow:**

1. **Actor:** Opens *My Profile*.
2. **System:** Displays the current display name, bio and profile picture.
3. **Actor:** Selects *Edit*, changes one or more fields and/or uploads a new picture, and saves.
4. **System:** Validates the input and saves the changes.
5. **System:** Displays the updated profile with a confirmation message.

**Alternative flows:**

- **A1 — Invalid input (branches from step 4):**
  1. A field is invalid (e.g., the picture has a disallowed type or size).
  2. The system shows a field-level message and saves nothing.
  3. The flow returns to step 3.
- **A2 — User cancels editing (branches from step 3):**
  1. The user selects *Cancel*.
  2. The system discards the changes and shows the unchanged profile.

**Exception / error flows (if applicable):**

- **E1 — Attempt to edit another user's profile (occurs at step 4):** The request targets another user's profile; the server returns HTTP 403 and nothing changes.

**Post-condition(s):**  
The user's profile contains the new values; for musicians, the changes are visible on the public artist profile (UC-05).

#### 3.4.6 UC-05 — View a Musician's Profile

| Field | Description |
|---|---|
| **Use case ID** | UC-05 |
| **Use case name** | View a musician's profile |
| **Goal / Purpose** | A listener wants to see who a musician is and all of the musician's releases. |
| **Actor(s)** | UT-02 — Listener (any logged-in user) |
| **Related Project Plan task(s)** | T-04 |
| **Related functional requirement(s)** | FR-13 |

**Pre-condition(s):**  
The user is logged in; the musician account exists and is active.

**Main success flow:**

1. **Actor:** Selects a musician's name (from search results, a song, the player or a room).
2. **System:** Displays the musician's public profile: display name, bio, picture, albums and songs.
3. **Actor:** Selects an album or song.
4. **System:** Shows the album's track list or starts the song (continues in UC-09).

**Alternative flows:**

- **A1 — Musician has no releases yet (branches from step 2):**
  1. The musician has not published any songs.
  2. The system shows the profile with a "no releases yet" message; the use case ends.

**Exception / error flows (if applicable):**

- **E1 — Profile not available (occurs at step 2):** The musician account was deactivated or does not exist; the system shows a "profile not found" page.

**Post-condition(s):**  
The user has seen the musician's public information and releases. No data is changed.

#### 3.4.7 UC-06 — Manage Songs and Albums

| Field | Description |
|---|---|
| **Use case ID** | UC-06 |
| **Use case name** | Manage songs and albums |
| **Goal / Purpose** | The musician wants to publish their music with correct metadata and keep it up to date. |
| **Actor(s)** | UT-03 — Musician (primary); UT-05 — Admin (removal path only) |
| **Related Project Plan task(s)** | T-05, T-03 |
| **Related functional requirement(s)** | FR-14, FR-15, FR-16, FR-11 |

**Pre-condition(s):**  
The user is logged in with a musician account (or an admin account for A4).

**Main success flow:**

1. **Actor:** Opens *My Music* and selects *New album*.
2. **Actor:** Enters the album title, genre and release date and selects a cover image.
3. **System:** Validates the data, uploads the cover (includes UC-07) and creates the album.
4. **Actor:** Selects *New song* and enters title and genre, chooses the album and track number, and selects the audio file.
5. **System:** Validates the required fields, uploads the audio (includes UC-07), records the duration and creates the song.
6. **System:** Shows the new album and song in *My Music* and on the musician's public profile; the song becomes searchable.

**Alternative flows:**

- **A1 — Single without album (branches from step 1):**
  1. The musician selects *New song* directly without creating an album.
  2. The flow continues at step 4 with no album selected.
- **A2 — Edit metadata (branches from step 1):**
  1. The musician selects an existing song or album and changes its metadata.
  2. The system validates and saves the change; the use case ends.
- **A3 — Delete own content (branches from step 1):**
  1. The musician selects *Delete* on an own song or album and confirms.
  2. The system removes it from the catalogue and its files from storage; the use case ends.
- **A4 — Admin removes content (branches from step 1):**
  1. An admin selects any song or album that violates copyright (e.g., after a report in UC-19) and chooses *Remove*.
  2. The system removes it; it no longer appears in search, profiles, queues or rooms.
  3. The system deactivates the account that uploaded it; the user cannot request reactivation or approval from the admin.

**Exception / error flows (if applicable):**

- **E1 — Missing required field (occurs at steps 3 or 5):** The system shows a validation message for each missing field and creates nothing; the musician corrects the form.
- **E2 — Content owned by another musician (occurs in A2/A3):** The server returns HTTP 403 and nothing changes.

**Post-condition(s):**  
The catalogue contains the musician's albums and songs with valid metadata and stored files, or the deleted/removed items are no longer accessible.

#### 3.4.8 UC-07 — Upload Audio and Cover Files

| Field | Description |
|---|---|
| **Use case ID** | UC-07 |
| **Use case name** | Upload audio and cover files |
| **Goal / Purpose** | The musician wants their audio and artwork stored safely so that listeners can play and see them. |
| **Actor(s)** | UT-03 — Musician (primary); UT-07 — Azure Blob Storage (secondary) |
| **Related Project Plan task(s)** | T-06 |
| **Related functional requirement(s)** | FR-17, FR-18, FR-19 (NFR-04, NFR-06, NFR-14, NFR-20) |

**Pre-condition(s):**  
The musician is creating or editing a song or album in UC-06.

**Main success flow:**

1. **Actor:** Selects an audio file (or a cover image) from their device.
2. **Actor:** For audio, ticks the confirmation that they hold the rights to distribute it, and submits.
3. **System:** Validates the file type against the allowed list and the size against the configured limit.
4. **System:** Uploads the file to Azure Blob Storage and shows upload progress.
5. **System:** Links the stored file to the song or album and confirms success.

**Alternative flows:**

- **A1 — Rights not confirmed (branches from step 2):**
  1. The musician submits without ticking the rights confirmation.
  2. The system rejects the upload and explains that confirmation is required; the flow returns to step 2.
- **A2 — Disallowed type or too large (branches from step 3):**
  1. The file fails validation.
  2. The system shows the allowed types and the size limit; nothing is uploaded; the flow returns to step 1.
- **A3 — Musician cancels the upload (branches from step 4):**
  1. The musician cancels while the file is uploading.
  2. The system stops the upload, discards any partial file and creates no song record.

**Exception / error flows (if applicable):**

- **E1 — Storage or network failure (occurs at step 4):** The system shows an error message, discards partial data and creates no song record pointing to a missing file; the musician can retry.

**Post-condition(s):**  
The file is stored in Azure Blob Storage (not publicly listable) and linked to the song or album.

#### 3.4.9 UC-08 — Search and Browse the Catalogue

| Field | Description |
|---|---|
| **Use case ID** | UC-08 |
| **Use case name** | Search and browse the catalogue |
| **Goal / Purpose** | The listener wants to find a specific song, album or musician, or discover new music. |
| **Actor(s)** | UT-02 — Listener |
| **Related Project Plan task(s)** | T-07, T-01 |
| **Related functional requirement(s)** | FR-01, FR-20, FR-21, FR-22 (NFR-07, NFR-11) |

**Pre-condition(s):**  
The user is logged in.

**Main success flow:**

1. **Actor:** Opens the homepage through the navigation bar.
2. **System:** Displays newly added songs and albums.
3. **Actor:** Enters a keyword in the search bar.
4. **System:** Returns matching songs, albums and musicians grouped by type.
5. **Actor:** Selects a result.
6. **System:** Shows the selected album or musician page, or starts the song (UC-09).

**Alternative flows:**

- **A1 — Browse by genre (branches from step 3):**
  1. The listener opens *Browse* and selects a genre.
  2. The system shows the first page of songs and albums in that genre.
  3. The listener moves to the next page; the system shows the next results. The flow continues at step 5.
- **A2 — No results (branches from step 4):**
  1. Nothing matches the keyword.
  2. The system shows a "no results" message and suggests browsing by genre; the flow returns to step 3.

**Exception / error flows (if applicable):**

- **E1 — Search service error (occurs at step 4):** The system shows an error message with a retry option; the rest of the application stays usable.

**Post-condition(s):**  
The listener has found the content they were looking for or has been told that none matches. No data is changed.

#### 3.4.10 UC-09 — Play a Track

| Field | Description |
|---|---|
| **Use case ID** | UC-09 |
| **Use case name** | Play a track |
| **Goal / Purpose** | The listener wants to listen to a song and control playback. |
| **Actor(s)** | UT-02 — Listener (primary); UT-07 — Azure Blob Storage (secondary) |
| **Related Project Plan task(s)** | T-08 |
| **Related functional requirement(s)** | FR-23, FR-24, FR-25, FR-35, FR-53 (NFR-04, NFR-10, NFR-14) |

**Pre-condition(s):**  
The user is logged in and has selected a song (e.g., from UC-05 or UC-08).

**Main success flow:**

1. **Actor:** Presses play on a song.
2. **System:** Obtains a time-limited streaming URL and starts playback within 2 s.
3. **System:** Shows title, musician, cover and elapsed/total time in the player bar, records a *play start* event (includes UC-14) and keeps the current track and position in the recovery log during playback.
4. **Actor:** Uses pause, seek and volume controls as needed.
5. **System:** Applies each control; seeking loads the requested position via a range request.
6. **System:** When the song ends, records a *completion* event and stops (or continues with the queue, A1).

**Alternative flows:**

- **A1 — Play queue (branches from step 4):**
  1. The listener adds songs to the queue.
  2. When the current song ends, or the listener presses *next*, the system plays the next queued song and returns to step 3. *Previous* restarts or returns to the previous song.
- **A2 — Skip (branches from step 4):**
  1. The listener skips the current song before it ends.
  2. The system records a *skip* event and plays the next queued song, if any.
- **A3 — Resume after being offline (branches from step 1):**
  1. The user comes back online or reopens the application after a disconnection during playback.
  2. The system reads the recovery log and offers to resume the same track at the saved position.
  3. If the user accepts, playback continues from that position and the flow returns to step 3; listening events created while offline are sent to the server.

**Exception / error flows (if applicable):**

- **E1 — Stream fails (occurs at step 2 or 5):** The file cannot be loaded or the network fails. The player shows an error with a retry option; the rest of the application stays usable.
- **E2 — URL expired (occurs at step 5):** The client requests a new time-limited URL and resumes at the same position.

**Post-condition(s):**  
The song has been played (fully or partly) and the matching listening events are recorded.

#### 3.4.11 UC-10 — Create a Listening Room

| Field | Description |
|---|---|
| **Use case ID** | UC-10 |
| **Use case name** | Create a listening room |
| **Goal / Purpose** | The user wants a shared space where friends can listen and chat together. |
| **Actor(s)** | UT-02 — Listener (becomes UT-04 — Room host) |
| **Related Project Plan task(s)** | T-09 |
| **Related functional requirement(s)** | FR-26, FR-50 |

**Pre-condition(s):**  
The user is logged in.

**Main success flow:**

1. **Actor:** Opens *Rooms* and selects *Create room*.
2. **Actor:** Enters a room name and confirms.
3. **System:** Validates the name, creates the room and makes the creator its host.
4. **System:** Opens the room page with the creator in the participant list and adds the room to the list of active rooms.

**Alternative flows:**

- **A1 — Empty or invalid name (branches from step 3):**
  1. The name is empty or invalid.
  2. The system shows a validation message; the flow returns to step 2.
- **A2 — Private room (branches from step 2) *(Should, FR-50)*:**
  1. The user chooses *Private* as the room type and enters a password.
  2. The system creates the room as private; joining it requires the password. The flow continues at step 3.

**Exception / error flows (if applicable):**

- **E1 — Real-time connection cannot be established (occurs at step 4):** The room is created but the WebSocket connection fails; the system shows a connection error and retries automatically (NFR-13).

**Post-condition(s):**  
An active room exists with the creator as host and only participant, and other users can see it in the room list.

#### 3.4.12 UC-11 — Join and Leave a Listening Room

| Field | Description |
|---|---|
| **Use case ID** | UC-11 |
| **Use case name** | Join and leave a listening room |
| **Goal / Purpose** | The user wants to enter a room to listen with others, and leave when finished. |
| **Actor(s)** | UT-02 — Listener |
| **Related Project Plan task(s)** | T-09, T-10, T-11 |
| **Related functional requirement(s)** | FR-08, FR-27, FR-28, FR-29, FR-31, FR-33, FR-49, FR-50, FR-51 (NFR-09, NFR-13) |

**Pre-condition(s):**  
The user is logged in and at least one room is active.

**Main success flow:**

1. **Actor:** Opens *Rooms*.
2. **System:** Shows active rooms with name, type (public/private), host, number of participants and current track.
3. **Actor:** Selects a public room and joins it without a password.
4. **System:** Checks that the room has fewer than 10 participants, opens an authenticated WebSocket connection, adds the user to the participant list and updates the list for all participants.
5. **System:** Shows the chat messages from the last hour and, if a track is playing, starts the user's playback at the room's current track and position.
6. **Actor:** Later selects *Leave room*.
7. **System:** Removes the user from the room, updates the participant list for the others and closes the user's room connection.

**Alternative flows:**

- **A1 — Host leaves (branches from step 7):**
  1. The leaving user is the host.
  2. The system transfers the host role to another participant and notifies everyone.
- **A2 — Last participant leaves (branches from step 7):**
  1. No participants remain.
  2. The system closes the room and removes it from the room list.
- **A3 — No active rooms (branches from step 2):**
  1. The list is empty.
  2. The system shows a message and offers *Create room* (UC-10).
- **A4 — Search and join a private room (branches from step 3) *(Should, FR-50, FR-51)*:**
  1. The user types the room name into the search field of the room list.
  2. The system shows the matching rooms.
  3. The user selects the private room and enters its password.
  4. The system verifies the password; the flow continues at step 4.

**Exception / error flows (if applicable):**

- **E1 — Invalid token (occurs at step 4):** The WebSocket connection is refused; the user is asked to log in again.
- **E2 — Connection lost (occurs while in the room):** Other participants see the user as disconnected; the client reconnects automatically and restores presence, chat and playback position (NFR-13). If reconnection is not possible, the user is shown as having left.
- **E3 — Room closed meanwhile (occurs at step 3):** The system shows "room no longer available" and refreshes the list.
- **E4 — Room is full (occurs at step 4):** The room already has 10 participants; the system rejects the join with a "room is full" message and the user stays on the room list.
- **E5 — Wrong password (occurs in A4, step 4):** The system rejects the join and asks the user to enter the password again.

**Post-condition(s):**  
After joining, the user is a participant, visible to all, and in sync with the room. After leaving, the user is no longer listed and the room has a host or has been closed.

#### 3.4.13 UC-12 — Chat in a Listening Room

| Field | Description |
|---|---|
| **Use case ID** | UC-12 |
| **Use case name** | Chat in a listening room |
| **Goal / Purpose** | The participant wants to talk with the others in the room in real time. |
| **Actor(s)** | UT-02 — Listener (room participant) |
| **Related Project Plan task(s)** | T-10 |
| **Related functional requirement(s)** | FR-30, FR-31 (NFR-08) |

**Pre-condition(s):**  
The user is a participant of a room (UC-11) with an active WebSocket connection.

**Main success flow:**

1. **Actor:** Types a message and sends it.
2. **System:** Checks that the sender is a participant of the room and that the message is not empty.
3. **System:** Stores the message and delivers it over WebSocket to all current participants of that room in under 300 ms.
4. **System:** Displays the message with the sender's name and time on every participant's screen.

**Alternative flows:**

- **A1 — Empty message (branches from step 2):**
  1. The message is empty or only whitespace.
  2. The system does not send it; the flow returns to step 1.

**Exception / error flows (if applicable):**

- **E1 — Connection lost while sending (occurs at step 3):** The client marks the message as "not sent" and resends it after automatic reconnection, or lets the user retry.
- **E2 — Sender is not a participant (occurs at step 2):** The server rejects the message (e.g., a user who has already left).

**Post-condition(s):**  
The message is stored in the room's chat history and is shown to the room's participants, including those who join later, for one hour after it was sent.

#### 3.4.14 UC-13 — Control Synchronized Room Playback

| Field | Description |
|---|---|
| **Use case ID** | UC-13 |
| **Use case name** | Control synchronized room playback |
| **Goal / Purpose** | The host wants everyone in the room to hear the same track at the same moment. |
| **Actor(s)** | UT-04 — Room host |
| **Related Project Plan task(s)** | T-11 |
| **Related functional requirement(s)** | FR-32, FR-33, FR-34, FR-35 (NFR-09) |

**Pre-condition(s):**  
The host is in a room (UC-10/UC-11) and the catalogue contains playable tracks.

**Main success flow:**

1. **Actor:** Selects a track for the room and presses play.
2. **System:** Verifies that the sender is the host.
3. **System:** Streams the room audio to all participants over WebRTC, starting at the selected position, so that drift from the host is below 500 ms.
4. **System:** Records a *play start* event with the room context for each listening participant (includes UC-14).
5. **Actor:** Pauses, resumes or seeks.
6. **System:** Applies the same action on all participants' players.

**Alternative flows:**

- **A1 — Participant joins mid-track (branches from step 3):**
  1. A new participant joins (UC-11).
  2. The system starts that participant at the room's current position; the flow continues.
- **A2 — Track ends (branches from step 5):**
  1. The track finishes.
  2. The system records completion events and the room waits for the host's next selection.

**Exception / error flows (if applicable):**

- **E1 — Non-host sends a playback command (occurs at step 2):** The system rejects the command; no client's playback changes.
- **E2 — A participant drifts or loses connection (occurs at step 3 or 6):** The client resynchronizes to the host's position after reconnecting; other participants are not affected.
- **E3 — Track cannot be streamed (occurs at step 3):** Participants see an error; the host is asked to pick another track.

**Post-condition(s):**  
All connected participants play the host's selected track at the same position (within 500 ms), and listening events are recorded with room context.

#### 3.4.15 UC-14 — Record Listening Events

| Field | Description |
|---|---|
| **Use case ID** | UC-14 |
| **Use case name** | Record listening events |
| **Goal / Purpose** | The system collects reliable listening data so that musicians receive accurate statistics. |
| **Actor(s)** | UT-02 — Listener (indirectly, by playing music); triggered by the web player, the room player and the mobile player |
| **Related Project Plan task(s)** | T-12 |
| **Related functional requirement(s)** | FR-35, FR-36, FR-53 (NFR-18) |

**Pre-condition(s):**  
A logged-in user's playback starts, is skipped or completes (in UC-09, UC-13 or UC-16).

**Main success flow:**

1. **Actor:** Starts, skips or finishes a track.
2. **System:** The player sends an event of type *play start*, *skip* or *complete*.
3. **System:** Validates the event and stores it with track, listener, timestamp and context (individual or room).
4. **System:** Includes the event in the aggregated metrics (play counts, popular tracks, plays over time); a play is counted for the musician only after at least 30 seconds of listening.

**Alternative flows:**

- **A1 — Offline or temporary failure (branches from step 2):**
  1. The event cannot be sent immediately (e.g., the user is offline).
  2. The client keeps the event in the listening event log and sends it when the connection returns; each event is stored at most once. The recovery log is used to resume playback (UC-09, A3).

**Exception / error flows (if applicable):**

- **E1 — Invalid event (occurs at step 3):** Events for a non-existent track or from an unauthenticated client are rejected and not counted.

**Post-condition(s):**  
Each valid playback action is stored exactly once, and plays of at least 30 seconds are reflected in the musician's aggregated statistics.

#### 3.4.16 UC-15 — View Musician Dashboard

| Field | Description |
|---|---|
| **Use case ID** | UC-15 |
| **Use case name** | View musician dashboard |
| **Goal / Purpose** | The musician wants to understand how their music is being listened to. |
| **Actor(s)** | UT-03 — Musician |
| **Related Project Plan task(s)** | T-13 |
| **Related functional requirement(s)** | FR-36, FR-37, FR-38, FR-39 (NFR-18) |

**Pre-condition(s):**  
The musician is logged in.

**Main success flow:**

1. **Actor:** Opens *Dashboard*.
2. **System:** Verifies the musician role and retrieves aggregated statistics for the musician's own tracks.
3. **System:** Displays total plays, play count per track, top tracks and a plays-over-time chart.
4. **Actor:** Selects a different time range.
5. **System:** Recalculates and redisplays all figures for that range.

**Alternative flows:**

- **A1 — No plays yet (branches from step 3):**
  1. The musician has no songs or no recorded plays.
  2. The system shows empty charts with an explanatory message; the use case ends.

**Exception / error flows (if applicable):**

- **E1 — Non-musician or other musician's data (occurs at step 2):** A listener opening the dashboard, or a request for another musician's statistics, is rejected with HTTP 403.
- **E2 — Analytics service error (occurs at step 2):** The system shows an error message with a retry option.

**Post-condition(s):**  
The musician has seen aggregated statistics about their own music only; no individual listener data was exposed.

#### 3.4.17 UC-16 — Use Core Features on Mobile

| Field | Description |
|---|---|
| **Use case ID** | UC-16 |
| **Use case name** | Use core features on mobile |
| **Goal / Purpose** | The listener wants to log in, find and play music on their phone. |
| **Actor(s)** | UT-02 — Listener (UT-01 — Guest when logging in) |
| **Related Project Plan task(s)** | T-14 |
| **Related functional requirement(s)** | FR-40, FR-41, FR-42, FR-35 (NFR-10, NFR-22) |

**Pre-condition(s):**  
The mobile app is installed on the chosen platform and the user has an account.

**Main success flow:**

1. **Actor:** Opens the app and logs in with their existing account.
2. **System:** Authenticates the user against the deployed API and shows the home screen.
3. **Actor:** Searches for or browses to a song.
4. **System:** Shows matching results from the same catalogue as the web.
5. **Actor:** Selects a song and presses play; uses pause and seek.
6. **System:** Streams the song, applies the controls and records listening events (includes UC-14).
7. **Actor:** Logs out when finished; the system invalidates the token.

**Alternative flows:**

- **A1 — Invalid credentials (branches from step 2):**
  1. Login fails; the app shows the generic error message and the flow returns to step 1.
- **A2 — No results (branches from step 4):**
  1. Nothing matches; the app shows a "no results" message and the flow returns to step 3.

**Exception / error flows (if applicable):**

- **E1 — No network connection (occurs at any step):** The app shows an offline message and lets the user retry when the connection is back.

**Post-condition(s):**  
The user has completed the login → search → play flow on mobile using the same account and catalogue as the web.

#### 3.4.18 UC-17 — Follow Users

| Field | Description |
|---|---|
| **Use case ID** | UC-17 |
| **Use case name** | Follow users |
| **Goal / Purpose** | The user wants to follow other users so that they can easily find the people they listen with. |
| **Actor(s)** | UT-02 — Listener (any logged-in user) |
| **Related Project Plan task(s)** | T-04 |
| **Related functional requirement(s)** | FR-45, FR-46 |

**Pre-condition(s):**  
The user is logged in and has opened another user's profile.

**Main success flow:**

1. **Actor:** Selects *Follow* on the other user's profile.
2. **System:** Adds the other user to the user's following list and adds the user to the other user's followers list; no approval is needed.
3. **System:** Changes the button to *Following* and updates the follower count shown on the profile.

**Alternative flows:**

- **A1 — Unfollow (branches from step 1):**
  1. The user selects *Following* (or *Unfollow* in their following list) for a user they already follow.
  2. The system removes that user from the following list and the user from that user's followers list; the use case ends.
- **A2 — View following and followers (branches from step 1):**
  1. The user opens their own profile and selects *Following* or *Followers*.
  2. The system shows the corresponding list of users; the user can open any of their profiles.

**Exception / error flows (if applicable):**

- **E1 — Already following or own profile (occurs at step 2):** The system does not create a duplicate follow, and the *Follow* option is not shown on the user's own profile.

**Post-condition(s):**  
The user follows the other user (or no longer follows them after unfollowing), and both users' following/followers lists reflect the change.

#### 3.4.19 UC-18 — Create and Manage Playlists

| Field | Description |
|---|---|
| **Use case ID** | UC-18 |
| **Use case name** | Create and manage playlists |
| **Goal / Purpose** | The user wants to group songs into playlists and, if they wish, show them on their profile. |
| **Actor(s)** | UT-02 — Listener (any logged-in user) |
| **Related Project Plan task(s)** | T-08, T-04 |
| **Related functional requirement(s)** | FR-47, FR-48 |

**Pre-condition(s):**  
The user is logged in.

**Main success flow:**

1. **Actor:** Opens *My Playlists* and selects *New playlist*.
2. **Actor:** Enters a playlist name and confirms.
3. **System:** Creates the empty playlist, owned by the user and not displayed on the profile.
4. **Actor:** Adds songs to the playlist from search results, album pages or the player.
5. **System:** Saves the songs in the playlist in the order they were added.
6. **Actor:** Plays the playlist.
7. **System:** Plays the songs in order (continues in UC-09).

**Alternative flows:**

- **A1 — Display on profile (branches from step 3):**
  1. The user turns on *Show on my profile* for the playlist.
  2. The system shows the playlist on the user's public profile; other users can open and play it.
  3. Turning the option off hides it again.
- **A2 — Edit or delete (branches from step 4):**
  1. The user removes songs, renames the playlist or deletes it.
  2. The system saves the change; a deleted playlist disappears everywhere, including the profile.

**Exception / error flows (if applicable):**

- **E1 — Empty name (occurs at step 3):** The system shows a validation message and creates nothing.
- **E2 — Song removed from the catalogue (occurs at step 7):** A song removed by its musician or an admin is no longer playable; the system skips it.

**Post-condition(s):**  
The playlist exists with the chosen songs and is visible on the profile only if the owner chose to display it.

#### 3.4.20 UC-19 — Report and Handle a Copyright Violation

| Field | Description |
|---|---|
| **Use case ID** | UC-19 |
| **Use case name** | Report and handle a copyright violation |
| **Goal / Purpose** | A user wants to report a song that violates copyright, and the admin wants to remove violating content and the account that uploaded it. |
| **Actor(s)** | UT-02 — Listener (reporter, any logged-in user); UT-05 — Admin |
| **Related Project Plan task(s)** | T-03, T-04, T-05 |
| **Related functional requirement(s)** | FR-52, FR-11, FR-10 |

**Pre-condition(s):**  
The reporter is logged in and has opened a musician's profile (UC-05).

**Main success flow:**

1. **Actor (reporter):** Selects *Report* on the musician's profile.
2. **Actor (reporter):** Writes which song the report is about and a short description of the violation, and submits.
3. **System:** Stores the report with the reporter, the musician and the text, confirms submission and adds it to the admin's report list.
4. **Actor (admin):** Opens the report list and reviews the report and the song.
5. **Actor (admin):** Confirms the violation and removes the song (UC-06, A4).
6. **System:** Removes the song from search, profiles, queues and rooms, deactivates the account that uploaded it and marks the report as resolved.

**Alternative flows:**

- **A1 — Report rejected (branches from step 5):**
  1. The admin finds no violation.
  2. The admin marks the report as rejected; the song and the account stay unchanged.

**Exception / error flows (if applicable):**

- **E1 — Empty report (occurs at step 3):** The song field or description is empty; the system shows a validation message and stores nothing.
- **E2 — Deactivated user tries to log in (after step 6):** The login is refused with a message that the account was deactivated for a copyright violation; the system offers no option to request reactivation or approval from the admin.

**Post-condition(s):**  
The report is stored and resolved; if a violation was confirmed, the song is no longer accessible and the uploader's account is permanently deactivated.

#### 3.4.21 UC-20 — Ask the Music-Discovery Assistant *(optional)*

| Field | Description |
|---|---|
| **Use case ID** | UC-20 |
| **Use case name** | Ask the music-discovery assistant |
| **Goal / Purpose** | The listener wants music suggestions by describing what they want in their own words. |
| **Actor(s)** | UT-02 — Listener (primary); UT-08 — External AI API (secondary) |
| **Related Project Plan task(s)** | T-18 (optional) |
| **Related functional requirement(s)** | FR-44 (NFR-19) |

**Pre-condition(s):**  
The feature was approved at the 11.12 go/no-go checkpoint; the user is logged in.

**Main success flow:**

1. **Actor:** Opens the assistant and types a request (e.g., "calm music for studying").
2. **System:** Sends the request, without personal data, to the external AI API together with catalogue information.
3. **System:** Matches the AI's answer against the Interlude catalogue and keeps only existing items.
4. **System:** Displays the suggestions with links to each song or album.
5. **Actor:** Selects a suggestion and plays it (continues in UC-09).

**Alternative flows:**

- **A1 — No matching catalogue items (branches from step 3):**
  1. None of the suggestions exists in the catalogue.
  2. The system tells the user it found nothing suitable and suggests rephrasing or browsing by genre.

**Exception / error flows (if applicable):**

- **E1 — AI API unavailable or over budget (occurs at step 2):** The system shows that the assistant is temporarily unavailable; the rest of the application is unaffected.

**Post-condition(s):**  
The user has received suggestions that exist in the catalogue, or a clear message that none were found; observed error types are logged for the AI evaluation report.
